provenance.original: TSA airport screening personnel monitor, transport, and store completed checkpoint log-in forms.  TSA estimates it takes a Supervisory Transportation Security Officer approximately 1.5 minutes (0.025 hours) to monitor, transport, and store forms per LEO checking-in for their pre-flight screening.  TSA estimates an average annual hour burden of 2,094 hours (6,281 of the 3-year window).  A Supervisory Transportation Security Officer has a fully-loaded wage rate of $75.94.  TSA estimates an average annual hour burden cost to TSA of $158,997 ($476,991 over 3 years).  This collection does not involve other federal entities; therefore, the TSA cost is the federal cost.  Table 2 summarizes these calculations.

provenance.original: (c) Compliance Recordkeeping Requirement.  TSA estimates that an average of 4 hours is required for each FAC to maintain copies and to make its security program available for review.  TSA assumes this task is done by a position equivalent to an Administrative Service Manager in the Air Transportation industry in the United States and takes the corresponding fully loaded hourly average wage rate of $94.71 as a proxy.  Based on information from past inspections, TSA estimates that each FAC has an average of 7 yearly inspections for compliance with the MSP.  TSA estimates that each inspection places a 4 hour burden on the carrier being inspected.  Therefore, TSA estimates an annual average hour burden of 5,350.  TSA estimates the average annual burden cost to be $506,721.

provenance.original: An aircraft operator may submit a request to TSA to change its TSA-approved security program or to adopt other means to meet the TSA-issued amendments.  Based on past requests, TSA estimates it will receive 120 requests annually.  TSA estimates 1 hour to prepare documentation for each request, for an annual burden of 120 hours (120 requests x 1 hour).  TSA uses the national average hourly loaded wage of $103.20 for General and Operations Managers to estimate the total annual hour burden cost of the requests to change the security programs.  The total annual hour burden cost due to the requests to change the security programs is estimated to be $12,384 ($103.20 x 120 hours).

provenance.original: (b) Carrier-Requested Security Program Amendments.  Under 49 CFR 1546.105(b), a FAC may submit a request to TSA through its assigned TSA International Industry Representative (IIR) to amend its TSA-accepted security program or adopt alternative procedures of complying with the TSA-issued amendments.  Based on past requests, TSA estimates that it receives on average of 83 requests annually from the population (180) of FACs.  TSA estimates that each FAC takes approximately 1 hour to prepare a document for each request and a Corporate Security Director or Security Manager completes the task, and assumes a fully loaded hourly average wage rate of $114.78. provenance.original: TSA also issues amendments and security directives to its security programs.  These amendments are either TSA-initiated or industry-requested. Industry-requested amendments typically are asking for approval from TSA for existing business practices, and TSA estimates a 1 hour each time burden for the 946 average annual industry requested amendments, for an annual hour burden of 946 hours. provenance.original: Designate a Cybersecurity Coordinator/Alternate Cybersecurity Coordinator: All Owner/Operators subject to this requirement have designated a Cybersecurity Coordinator and at least one alternate coordinator.  However, due to employee turnover, TSA anticipates that some entities will need to periodically designate new Cybersecurity Coordinators or alternates.  In these instances, TSA SMEs estimate respondents will spend 5 minutes (0.083 hours) performing this task.  TSA assumes that the designation of a new Cybersecurity Coordinator (or alternate) represents a small burden that only includes emailing TSA the names, titles, phone numbers, and email addresses of the new individual taking on that role.

provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.
